dimensions.assessment: The bill affects federal transportation officials, state and local governments, universities, and private sector entities involved in transportation research and materials production.
dimensions.evidence: Seek to consult with representatives from the Institutions of higher education, State departments of transportation, Units of local government

dimensions.assessment: The effects are primarily administrative and regulatory, involving research coordination, statistical standard updates, and reports on highway safety and asphalt materials.
dimensions.evidence: establish the Transportation Statistics Coordination Council... to coordinate statistical activities and evaluations across the Department.

dimensions.assessment: The source extends authorization timelines for existing research and technology programs through fiscal years 2027 through 2031 but does not specify new dollar appropriation amounts.
dimensions.evidence: striking fiscal years 2022 through 2026 and inserting fiscal years 2027 through 2031

dimensions.assessment: The legislation amends multiple sections of titles 23, 49, and other United States codes, establishes a new inter-agency council, and requires several specific studies and reports.
dimensions.evidence: establish the 'Transportation Statistics Coordination Council' (in this subsection referred to as the 'Council') to coordinate statistical activities

dimensions.assessment: Extends program authorities through 2031 and permanently updates organizational structures and duties within the Department of Transportation.

missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for authorized funding levels are not stated in the source text.
Exact staffing counts for the new council or committees are not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill extends existing surface transportation, research, and university transportation center programs through fiscal year 2031, establishes a Transportation Statistics Coordination Council, requires studies and reports on headlamp technologies and reclaimed asphalt pavement, and updates rail and open research programs. Its effects are moderate, focusing on federal transportation research administration, coordination, and reporting.
